title: I rented a cabin where the only rule was to leave one chair empty. I sat in it anyway.
story:
The host's note was taped to the table. Welcome. Four chairs, please use only three. Leave the one by the window empty.

There were three of us on the trip, me and two friends, so it was easy. We ate dinner, laughed, played cards. Nobody touched the chair by the window.

But all night I felt the room tilt toward it, the way you feel someone staring. Around midnight, my friend Mark made a joke about the rule. He stood up, crossed the room, and sat in the chair, just to prove nothing would happen.

Nothing happened. We all laughed. He sat for a full minute.

Then he stopped laughing, but his mouth kept moving.

"Don't sit anywhere else," he said, in a flat voice. "It took so long to find a place that fits."

Mark stood, perfectly slowly, and walked into the bedroom. We heard the door click.

In the morning his bed was made. His shoes were by the door. His phone was on the pillow.

The chair by the window was empty.

At the table there were four plates.

Three of us are left, and I can't remember which three.
premise: cabin with four chairs and three guests; the empty chair's occupant is revealed by who else sits
